version.changelog: v1.0.2 — fix installed skill path references (skills/imap-smtp-mail/)

llm.summary: The skill's code matches its stated IMAP/SMTP purpose, but the optional inbox-watcher spawns the OpenClaw agent and forwards email content (and the process environment) which creates a realistic data‑exfiltration / privacy risk that the user should explicitly acknowledge before enabling.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (read/send email via IMAP/SMTP) aligns with the provided scripts (imap.js, smtp.js, email-watch-lite.js) and setup helper. Requiring node/npm/openclaw is consistent with the watcher/alerting behavior described in SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs creating a local credentials file and running the Node scripts — expected. However the email watcher (email-watch-lite.js) invokes the 'openclaw' CLI (child_process.execFileSync) and builds an agent prompt containing email content to be analyzed; that will cause email bodies/attachments (and other context) to be sent to whatever agent backend OpenClaw uses. The README mentions forwarding but does not highlight the privacy/remote‑transmission implications or that the child process will be run with process.env forwarded.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec in registry; SKILL.md instructs running npm install in the skill folder. Dependencies are standard npm packages (imap, mailparser, nodemailer, pdf-parse, xlsx, dotenv). No downloads from nonstandard URLs are present in the provided files. This is moderate risk only because npm packages will be installed during setup (expected for a Node tool).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Registry metadata lists no required env vars, but the code expects a credentials file (~/.openclaw/credentials/imap-smtp-email.env) that contains IMAP/SMTP secrets and ALLOWED_READ_DIRS/ALLOWED_WRITE_DIRS. The watcher forwards process.env into the child openclaw process, so any credentials in environment or process env could be exposed to the invoked agent. Requesting no declared envs in registry while relying on a credentials file is an omission that can confuse users about what secrets will be used and where they live.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and no modifications to other skills. The skill writes its own credentials file via setup.sh and state under the workspace — expected. The larger concern is the combination of autonomous agent invocation (normal platform default) with the watcher's behavior: if enabled, the watcher can automatically trigger agent runs that analyze and forward email content.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to do what it says (read/send mail), but review these items before installing or enabling the inbox watcher:

- Understand where your IMAP/SMTP credentials will be stored: setup.sh writes them to ~/.openclaw/credentials/imap-smtp-email.env. Treat that file as sensitive and keep its permissions locked (the script sets 600).
- The optional watcher (email-watch-lite.js) will call the local 'openclaw' CLI to run an agent and will include email content in the agent prompt. If OpenClaw's agent backend is remote or if agents are configured to use external LLMs, your email bodies and attachment text may be sent off‑host. Only enable the watcher if you accept that risk.
- execFileSync is invoked with env: process.env — any secrets present in the environment could be exposed to the child process/agent. Avoid running the watcher in environments with unrelated secrets in environment variables.
- Confirm ALLOWED_READ_DIRS and ALLOWED_WRITE_DIRS are narrowly scoped to directories you control so attachments and files cannot be read from or written to unexpected locations.
- If you prefer to avoid remote analysis, do not enable the watcher or disable the trigger/forwarding behavior. You can still use the IMAP/SMTP scripts locally without the watcher.
- Use app-specific passwords where possible (e.g., Gmail App Passwords) rather than your primary account password.
- If you need higher assurance, run this skill in an isolated environment (dedicated VM/container) and audit network access for the 'openclaw' CLI/agent before allowing automatic forwarding.

If you want, I can: (a) point out the exact lines that forward mail to the agent, (b) suggest a safe configuration to disable the watcher, or (c) produce a minimal checklist for secure deployment.
llm.findings:
[child_process_execFileSync] expected: email-watch-lite.js uses execFileSync to run the local 'openclaw' CLI to send alerts/trigger agents. This is consistent with the described inbox-watcher feature, but it forwards process.env and may cause email content and environment variables to be transmitted to the agent/back-end.
[dotenv_load_env_file] expected: imap.js and smtp.js call dotenv to load credentials from ~/.openclaw/credentials/imap-smtp-email.env (configurable via EMAIL_ENV_FILE). This is expected, but those secrets are required for operation and are not declared as registry env requirements.
[filesystem_read_write] expected: The skill reads/writes state and attachments under the workspace and credentials under ~/.openclaw; scripts include path validation against ALLOWED_READ_DIRS/ALLOWED_WRITE_DIRS. This is consistent with functionality but depends on correct configuration of these whitelists.
